name: Shamrock Regional Park
note: Regional park in a horseshoe bend of the Wood River about 20 minutes northeast of Gravelbourg, with a pool, a nine-hole sand-green golf course and ball diamonds. Electric sites are mostly 15 A with a limited number of 30 A, and seasonal campers hold an unpublished share of the sites. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: shamrockregionalpark.ca read 2026-11-19 (live WordPress site, home page updated 2026-06-11 with 2026 events, swim lessons and pool season; RM of Shamrock #134 regional park, Box 113 Shamrock SK): '100 electrified sites many non electric sites and seasonal sites available', fees page (2025 rates) electric C$35 / non-electric C$30 daily with weekly, monthly and seasonal rates, '15 amp and limited 30 amp power sites', modern washrooms, drinking water, showers; Tourism Saskatchewan listing 2197 (75 electric + 40 non-electric sites, sewage disposal, 'Open May long weekend to Labour Day', 306-394-4269); Google Maps 'Shamrock Regional Park' 4.6 (28), phone 306-394-4269, website, open; SRPA 2026 guide lists Shamrock among the 2026 Non Accredited Regional Parks; Esri imagery 2026-11-19 shows ~45 trailers and fifth wheels of 30 ft+ on grass pads along the west side of the central field and in a wooded loop inside the river bend -> real drive-in public campground a 23-ft rig fits, nights sold at a posted daily rate with no application or lease; nightly share vs seasonal unmeasured. Local: no price gate. Not in DB (nearest entry 9233 Gravelbourg Town Campground, 21 km). (phase-7 SK lead 8, found p3-529) --Claude
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-19: Esri World Imagery read at 50.0595,-106.4640 (1 km frame), 50.0590,-106.4675 (400 m frame, camping core) and 50.0580,-106.4620 (400 m frame, south of the river), all rendered. The camping sits inside a horseshoe bend of the Wood River: the west row of trailers lines the inland edge of the open central field ~100-150 m from the river with a continuous tree belt on the bank between; the wooded SW loop's outer trailers come within ~40-55 m of the river but through dense trees and shrubs that fill the whole bank; a small cluster of trailers south of the river (east of the grid road bridge) sits under trees ~40-80 m from the water with a tree belt between. The operator publishes no site map, site numbers or campsite photos, so no nightly pad can be named; no open apron anywhere on the bend. Trees on the bank and no named nightly sites -> not waterfront (default down).

fees.note: Electric site C$35 a night, C$185 a week, C$485 a month or C$1,300 a season; non-electric C$30, C$125, C$245 or C$380. Park entry C$5 a day or a C$60 season sticker good at any Saskatchewan regional park. Extra tents C$20, extra fridges or freezers C$25, delivered potable water C$20. 2025 rates, still posted in November 2026.

flags: Nightly share unmeasured: the operator says '100 electrified sites many non electric sites and seasonal sites available' and posts daily, weekly, monthly and seasonal rates for both site types, but publishes no site map, count of seasonal sites or booking engine. Summer imagery shows ~45 trailers parked, many looking long-stay. If AWH wants the 1-in-10 test measured, it needs a phone answer (306-394-4269 in season, 306-648-3594 off season).

Booking group omitted: no reservation channel is published anywhere (no Let's Camp/Campspot listing; letscamp.ca/api/camps/shamrock-regional-park returns null). The policies page mentions a camping permit and a booth, so it is probably pay-on-arrival, but that is unstated.

Sites group omitted: the operator's '100 electrified sites' conflicts with Tourism Saskatchewan's 75 electric + 40 non-electric; no site lengths published anywhere (fit judged from imagery: trailers and fifth wheels of 30 ft+ on open grass pads).

Season group omitted: Tourism Saskatchewan says 'Open May long weekend to Labour Day'; the operator's banner (home page updated 2026-06-11) says full services until Sept 1, no service Sept 2-30, and trailers must be out by Sept 30; park phone 'Seasonal May Long - Sept Long'. No fixed opening date.
Water/sewer hookups not written: no source states them; the C$20 potable-water delivery to campers suggests sites have no water hookups.

Fees are the 2025 rates (fees page last modified 2025-03-30), still the only posted rates in November 2026. Entry fee left in fees.note rather than fees.entrance because the page does not say the C$5 day pass is per vehicle.

Not accredited: the SRPA 2026 guide lists Shamrock among the Non Accredited Regional Parks (saskregionalparks.ca/park/shamrock/ is 404), but the park is clearly operating: own site with June 2026 events, pool and swim lessons, Google 4.6 (28) with the park phone. The Google rating is the whole park's (pool, golf, ball tournaments), not the campground's alone.

Phone: 306-394-4269 is the park/concession phone (operator, Google and Tourism SK agree), staffed May long weekend to September long weekend; the lead's 306-648-3594 is the RM of Shamrock's off-season number.

Pin: Google (50.05921,-106.46362) and Tourism SK (50.05907,-106.4606) points sit at the entrance road/river crossing ~350-600 m east of the camping; pinned between the west trailer row and the wooded SW loop from Esri imagery. A small group of trailers also sits under trees south of the river near the grid-road bridge (~50.0582,-106.4620); whether that is campground, overflow or cabins is unknown.
General campground: no horse camping or OHV staging mentioned. No gateway within 40 km (not needed: local).
